newsitem.title: UK: Oil rigs exploring UK offshore to rise to 105 in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Oil rigs exploring UK offshore to rise to 105 in 1997.

text.p: Oil rigs exploring and appraising finds in the UK sector of the North Sea are forecast to rise by four to 105 this year, said analysts Wood Mackenzie.
There was an upturn in exploration and appraisal (E and A) drilling in 1996 after a period of decline that began in 1991, Wood MacKenzie said in a report.
Following 83 new well starts in 1995, which was the lowest level since 1981, there were 101 started in 1996.
The level of exploration drilling rose by 32 percent in 1996 over 1995 but appraisal drilling fell by 10 percent.
Despite the gains, E and A drilling was tempered in 1996 and 1995 by heavy development drilling schedules and the tight rig market.

Demand for mobile rigs rose six percent in 1996 to 42.8 rig years. One rig year represents one rig being operated for one year. The size of the fleet rose to 81 units from 75 units in January 1996 but strong demand meant that utilisation rates still reached 100 percent.
